context_lines.text: > **Measured density: ρ = 838.8 ± 0.4 kg/m³** (expanded uncertainty at 95% confidence)

claims.text: A second paper (DOI [10.1021/je800158z](https://doi.org/10.1021/je800158z)) measured the same system at a nearby composition (x = 0.5204) and bracketing temperatures (293.15 K and 303.15 K) at 81.5 kPa. Interpolating to 298.15 K gives ~835 kg/m³ at x = 0.5204, which is consistent with the reference value when accounting for the slightly higher propan-2-ol content (which lowers the density).

claims.text: The equimolar mixture is significantly **less dense** than the linear interpolation would predict, reflecting a **positive excess volume** (volume expansion upon mixing). This is characteristic of the propan-2-ol + water system, where the disruption of water's hydrogen-bonding network by the hydrophobic isopropyl group leads to less efficient molecular packing compared to the pure liquids. The excess volume is most pronounced in the alcohol-rich region, which is why the measured density (838.8 kg/m³) falls well below the ideal mixing prediction.
